title: Case #9: The Ghost in the Ledger
summary: The group-wide loyalty programme is paying welcome bonuses to someone who doesn't exist. Every skill you have, one last time.

steps.title: Case #9
body: Your last case. Larkspur's new **loyalty programme** pays a **£20 welcome bonus** to every new member, once per person, across all the businesses. In its first week the bonus budget is already blown.
Rosa slides the data across, the same way she did on your first day. *"Somebody's joining again and again. Find out who's really behind it."*
Tables: `loyalty_members(id, name, email, joined_at, meta)`, `welcome_bonuses(member_id, amount_cents, paid_on)`, `staff_codes(code, staff_name, department)`.
Email providers ignore anything between a `+` and the `@`: `r.quill+books@mail.test` and `r.quill@mail.test` reach the same inbox.

steps.title: Clue 1: one inbox, many members
prompt: Normalise each email: **trim** it, **lower-case** it, and **remove any `+tag`** from the part before the `@`. Then return each normalised **inbox** that belongs to more than one member, with the number of **members**, most first.

Tables: `loyalty_members(id, name, email, joined_at, meta)` (meta is JSON with `business`, `device`, `referrer`), `welcome_bonuses(member_id, amount_cents, paid_on)`, `staff_codes(code, staff_name, department)`.
solution: SELECT lower(trim(substr(trim(email), 1, CASE WHEN instr(email, '+') > 0 THEN instr(trim(email), '+') - 1 ELSE instr(trim(email), '@') - 1 END) || substr(trim(email), instr(trim(email), '@')))) AS inbox, COUNT(*) AS members
setup: CREATE TABLE loyalty_members (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, email TEXT, joined_at TEXT, meta TEXT);

steps.explain: Ana joined twice (an honest mistake: two businesses, two sign-ups). `r.quill@mail.test` joined **five** times, once per business.

steps.title: Clue 2: the device
prompt: For the members whose email contains **`r.quill`** (any case), return **id**, **business** and **device** from the JSON, and the **hour** they joined (`HH`, from `joined_at`), by id.

Tables: `loyalty_members(id, name, email, joined_at, meta)` (meta is JSON with `business`, `device`, `referrer`), `welcome_bonuses(member_id, amount_cents, paid_on)`, `staff_codes(code, staff_name, department)`.
solution: SELECT id, meta ->> '$.business' AS business, meta ->> '$.device' AS device, strftime('%H', joined_at) AS hour

steps.explain: Same device `dev-77f` every time, always between 3 and 4 in the morning, one business per night.

steps.title: Clue 3: a five-night streak
prompt: Treat each day `dev-77f` was used to join as a row. Using the gaps-and-islands trick, return the streak: **start**, **finish** and **nights**.

Tables: `loyalty_members(id, name, email, joined_at, meta)` (meta is JSON with `business`, `device`, `referrer`), `welcome_bonuses(member_id, amount_cents, paid_on)`, `staff_codes(code, staff_name, department)`.
solution: SELECT DISTINCT date(joined_at) AS day FROM loyalty_members WHERE meta ->> '$.device' = 'dev-77f'
SELECT day, date(day, '-' || ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY day) || ' days') AS grp FROM d
SELECT MIN(day) AS start, MAX(day) AS finish, COUNT(*) AS nights

steps.explain: Five nights in a row, November 2nd to 6th. That's a routine, not an accident: £100 in bonuses.

steps.title: Name the culprit
prompt: Every one of those sign-ups used the same **referrer** code from the JSON, and referrer codes starting with `STAFF-` belong to employees. Return the **staff_name** and **department** behind the referrer used by `dev-77f`, and the total bonus paid to those accounts (**bonus_cents**).

Tables: `loyalty_members(id, name, email, joined_at, meta)` (meta is JSON with `business`, `device`, `referrer`), `welcome_bonuses(member_id, amount_cents, paid_on)`, `staff_codes(code, staff_name, department)`.
solution: SELECT s.staff_name, s.department, SUM(b.amount_cents) AS bonus_cents
JOIN staff_codes AS s ON s.code = m.meta ->> '$.referrer'
JOIN welcome_bonuses AS b ON b.member_id = m.id

steps.explain: **Corin Ashby**, who runs the loyalty programme, created five fake members on his own device at 3 a.m., each referred by his own staff code, and pocketed £100 in welcome bonuses plus his referral rewards. Rosa closes the laptop. *"Nine cases. You don't need me looking over your shoulder any more."*
